title: Models of opinion formation combining network adaptation and opinion adoption (arXiv physics/0603023)

key_points.claim: Opinion-convergence models fall into two classes: opinions shaped by network neighbors, versus network ties forming between individuals with similar beliefs.
key_points.evidence_quote: These models divide into two classes, those in which individuals form their beliefs based on the opinions of their neighbors in a social network of personal acquaintances, and those in which, conversely, network connections form between individuals of similar beliefs.

key_points.claim: The paper proposes a combined model with a single parameter balancing the two processes, arguing real opinion formation involves both.
key_points.evidence_quote: Here we present a simple model of this combination, with a single parameter controlling the balance of the two processes.

key_points.claim: The model shows a continuous phase transition from diverse opinions to consensus-like majority agreement as the parameter varies.
key_points.evidence_quote: the model undergoes a continuous phase transition as this parameter is varied, from a regime in which opinions are arbitrarily diverse to one in which most individuals hold the same opinion.

reliability_notes: Abstract only. The arXiv preprint is from 2006 and its full text was not retrieved. The abstract does not name the authors or say whether the model is agent-based, although it is an agent-like network model.
